praesegmen , ĭnis, n. praeseco,
I.a piece cut off, a paring (ante- and postclass.): “tonsor omnia abstulit praesegmina,” Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 33 ; cf.: “praesegmina proprie Plautus in Aululariā ea dici voluit, quae unguibus eminulis praesecantur,” Non. 151, 33 : “cadaverum,” App. M. 2, p. 123, 24 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
